project.name: llm4s-chain
project.description: Scala 3, cats-effect/sttp building blocks for LLM applications: provider-neutral chat + tool calling, typed structured outputs, streaming, memory, RAG, agentic workflows, MCP tools, guardrails, and multimodals.

nodes.name: ci.yml
nodes.summary: GitHub Actions CI workflow that runs on push and pull_request to main/master, executing lint, compile, test, and code coverage reporting for the llm4s-chain Scala 3 project using sbt on a matrix of Scala 3.3.4 and Java 21.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses a matrix strategy over Scala and Java versions with fail-fast disabled; caches Ivy2, sbt, and Coursier for faster builds; uploads JUnit XML test results and Codecov coverage reports.

nodes.name: lint-compile-and-test
nodes.summary: Single CI job that sequentially checks out code, sets up Java 21 and sbt, caches dependencies, runs pre-commit hooks, compiles and tests with scalafmt check, uploads JUnit results, and generates scoverage + Codecov reports.

nodes.name: .env.llm4s-chain
nodes.summary: Environment variable template defining API keys and endpoint configuration for LLM providers (OpenAI, Anthropic, etc.) used by the llm4s-chain project.

nodes.name: .pre-commit-config.yaml
nodes.summary: Pre-commit hook configuration referencing local hooks from `.pre-commit-hooks.yaml` with default stages set for all commits.

nodes.name: .pre-commit-hooks.yaml
nodes.summary: Defines two pre-commit hook entries — ScalaFmt and ScalaFix — automating Scala code formatting and lint rules on every commit.

nodes.name: AGENTS.md
nodes.summary: Short guidance document for AI coding agents interacting with this repository, covering the graphify skill invocation pattern.

nodes.name: CHANGELOG.md
nodes.summary: Comprehensive development changelog tracking 17 completed PRs that built the Native Scala 3 LLM framework from core ADTs through streaming, RAG, agentic workflows, MCP, guardrails, and multimodal support, plus post-roadmap cleanup and per-module review findings.
nodes.languageNotes: Structured around a PR-based delivery plan with 4-tier module dependency ordering (core → single-dep → chat-execution-stack → capabilities).

nodes.name: CODE_REVIEW.md
nodes.summary: Detailed code review document listing 17 numbered issues across typed error handling, effect constraints, ToolKit design, tool derivation, resource discipline, parallel execution, telemetry, and naming, with a recommended fix order.

nodes.name: LCEL_DRAFT_PLAN.md
nodes.summary: Draft design plan for an LCEL-style composable DSL in Scala 3, defining the `Runnable[F,I,O]` abstraction, first-class nodes, combinators, a 6-phase delivery plan, 8 resolved design decisions, and acceptance criteria.
nodes.languageNotes: Draws explicit parallels to LangChain Expression Language (LCEL) while leveraging cats-effect typed effects and Scala 3 type-safety.

nodes.name: README.md
nodes.summary: Primary project README providing an overview of the llm4s-chain Scala 3 LLM framework, listing module capabilities (chat, tools, streaming, memory, RAG, workflows, MCP, guardrails, multimodal) and quick-start usage examples.

nodes.name: README_2026-05-18.md
nodes.summary: Dated repository review from 2026-05-18 cataloguing 44 findings across HIGH (15), MEDIUM (18), and LOW (11) severity categories, covering listener errors, concurrency bugs in memory, streaming defects, MCP protocol gaps, and CI misconfiguration.

nodes.name: README_ANTI_G_2026-05-21.md
nodes.summary: Short roadmap document outlining 5 traceability improvements for the anti-G branch: OTEL integration, MCP context propagation, token/cost metrics, DSL graph telemetry, and payload masking.

nodes.name: config.yaml
nodes.summary: Runtime application configuration covering LLM provider settings (model, temperature, max-tokens, provider selection), logging levels, and tracing/telemetry endpoint configuration.

nodes.name: readme_2026-05-17.md
nodes.summary: Dated repository review from 2026-05-17 identifying 8 findings including a silent parallel guardrail bug, unsafe StdioMcpTransport under parallel tool execution, MCP response-id validation gap, CI misconfiguration, incomplete streaming surface, and spurious Authorization header.

nodes.name: ua-import-map-input.json
nodes.summary: Input manifest for the understand-anything import resolution step, listing the project root and the full set of source files to be analyzed for cross-file import relationships.
nodes.languageNotes: Generated at analysis time; top-level keys are projectRoot and files (array of file descriptors).

nodes.name: ua-import-map-output.json
nodes.summary: Output of the understand-anything import-map script, recording resolved inter-file import relationships (importMap) and processing statistics for the llm4s-chain project.
nodes.languageNotes: Top-level keys: scriptCompleted (boolean), stats (counts), importMap (file-to-imports mapping).

nodes.name: ua-scan-files.json
nodes.summary: Output of the understand-anything project file scanner, enumerating all discovered source files with their language, size, and category metadata, plus aggregate scan statistics and complexity estimates.
nodes.languageNotes: Top-level keys: scriptCompleted, files (array of file descriptors), totalFiles, filteredByIgnore, estimatedComplexity, stats.

nodes.name: hooks.json
nodes.summary: Codex hooks configuration defining lifecycle hooks for the AI coding assistant, scoped to this project.

nodes.name: .envrc
nodes.summary: direnv environment file that loads project-specific shell environment variables when entering the project directory.

nodes.name: .sbtopts
nodes.summary: SBT JVM options file providing default JVM flags (e.g. heap size) applied whenever sbt is launched in this project.

nodes.name: .scalafmt.conf
nodes.summary: Scalafmt code-formatting configuration specifying the Scala dialect, line width, and style rules applied project-wide.
nodes.languageNotes: Scalafmt is the standard Scala formatter; the dialect setting must match the Scala version in build.sbt.

nodes.name: .understandignore
nodes.summary: Ignore-patterns file for the understand-anything scanner, listing paths and glob patterns that should be excluded from codebase analysis.

nodes.name: scan-result.json
nodes.summary: Machine-generated project scan result produced by the understand-anything scanner, containing the full file inventory, language breakdown, frameworks, import map, and complexity estimates.

nodes.name: build.sbt
nodes.summary: Root SBT multi-project build definition declaring all llm4s sub-modules, their inter-module dependencies, shared compiler settings, and an aggregate 'all' target for CI.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses a separate project/Dependencies.scala to centralise version pins (PR-15 convention). The flat classloader-layering strategy avoids Scala 3 inline-given LinkageErrors in test forks.

nodes.name: USAGE.md
nodes.summary: Comprehensive Scala 3 usage guide with 17 sections covering architecture, module map, provider setup, plain chat, AiAgent builder, tools, structured outputs, streaming, memory, RAG, agentic workflows, MCP tools, guardrails, multimodal requests, capability checks, and testing.

nodes.name: Agent.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the WorkflowAgent trait (a named In => F[Out] function with shared scope) and the backwards-compatible Agent type alias retained from the PR-17 rename; also provides AgentWorkflow, which adapts an agent into a Workflow.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses Scala 3 type alias (`type Agent = WorkflowAgent`) and a companion val alias so both the type and companion object keep working under the old name.

nodes.name: WorkflowAgent
nodes.summary: Core trait for a named, statically-typed workflow step; exposes run(input, scope): F[Out] and a convenience .workflow adapter.

nodes.name: AgentScope.scala
nodes.summary: Provides AgentScope, a thread-safe key-value store (backed by cats-effect Ref) that agents share across a single workflow run to pass intermediate results.
nodes.languageNotes: The private runtimeClass helper maps primitive Scala types to their boxed Java counterparts so ClassTag-based runtime casts work correctly for Int, Long, etc.

nodes.name: AgentScope
nodes.summary: Thread-safe shared blackboard for a workflow run; supports typed put/get with ClassTag reflection and full snapshot.

nodes.name: ConditionalWorkflow.scala
nodes.summary: Implements ConditionalWorkflow, which routes a workflow execution to one of two branches based on a boolean predicate evaluated in F.

nodes.name: ConditionalWorkflow
nodes.summary: Workflow combinator that evaluates a predicate and delegates to ifTrue or ifFalse sub-workflows accordingly.

nodes.name: LoopWorkflow.scala
nodes.summary: Implements LoopWorkflow, which iterates a body Workflow[F,A,A] using tailRecM for stack safety, stopping when a continuation predicate returns false or a maxIterations guard fires.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses cats tailRecM for guaranteed stack safety across arbitrarily many loop iterations.

nodes.name: LoopWorkflow
nodes.summary: Stack-safe loop combinator that re-runs a workflow body until a predicate stops it or maxIterations is exceeded, raising WorkflowError.MaxIterationsExceeded on overflow.

nodes.name: ParallelWorkflow.scala
nodes.summary: Implements ParallelWorkflow, which fans the same input out to two independent sub-workflows and collects their results as a tuple using cats Parallel.

nodes.name: ParallelWorkflow
nodes.summary: Workflow combinator that runs left and right branches concurrently via parTupled and returns (LeftOut, RightOut).

nodes.name: PlanStep.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the PlanStep and StepResult data types used by SupervisorAgent to represent individual steps in a dynamically constructed execution plan.

nodes.name: SequenceWorkflow.scala
nodes.summary: Implements SequenceWorkflow, which chains two workflows by feeding the output of the first as input to the second using flatMap.

nodes.name: SequenceWorkflow
nodes.summary: Sequential composition combinator that threads data through first then second workflow steps.

nodes.name: SubAgentRegistry.scala
nodes.summary: Defines SubAgentRegistry, an immutable map from agent name to Agent instance used by SupervisorAgent to look up sub-agents at runtime.

nodes.name: SupervisorAgent.scala
nodes.summary: Implements SupervisorAgent, an orchestrating agent that delegates to dynamically selected sub-agents by invoking a SupervisorPlanner to produce a PlanStep list and then executing each step via a SubAgentRegistry.

nodes.name: SupervisorAgent
nodes.summary: Orchestrating agent that calls a planner, executes each planned step via a registry lookup, stores results in scope, and reduces outputs with an aggregate function.

nodes.name: Workflow.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the Workflow[F,In,Out] trait — the fundamental composable unit of the agentic module — with an andThen combinator for sequential composition.

nodes.name: WorkflowError.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the WorkflowError sealed hierarchy with MaxIterationsExceeded (for LoopWorkflow) and MissingSubAgent (for SupervisorAgent) as typed domain errors.

nodes.name: WorkflowListener.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the WorkflowListener observability trait with noop and Default implementations, plus InstrumentedAgent — a decorator that wraps a WorkflowAgent to fire lifecycle events and measure wall-clock duration on each run.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses a Scala 3 extension method (instrumented) so callers can write agent.instrumented(listener) directly without importing a separate wrapper.

nodes.name: WorkflowListener
nodes.summary: Observability hook trait fired on agent start, success, and failure; sibling to RuntimeListener and GuardrailListener.

nodes.name: InstrumentedAgent
nodes.summary: Decorator over WorkflowAgent that fires WorkflowListener events and records nanosecond duration on every run call.

nodes.name: AgenticWorkflowSpec.scala
nodes.summary: munit test suite exercising all agentic workflow combinators — sequence, parallel, conditional, loop (happy path, max-iterations, stack safety), and supervisor agent (successful planning, missing sub-agent error).

nodes.name: WorkflowAgentRenameSpec.scala
nodes.summary: munit regression spec that locks in the PR-17 rename: verifies that WorkflowAgent and the legacy Agent alias are the same type and both construct correctly.

nodes.name: WorkflowListenerSpec.scala
nodes.summary: munit test suite for WorkflowListener and InstrumentedAgent, verifying event ordering on success, failure re-raise, and correct nesting inside sequence/parallel compositions.

nodes.name: AiContent.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the AiContent sealed trait and its three variants — Text, Image, and File — each carrying required ModelCapability flags for capability checking across providers.
nodes.languageNotes: Each variant declares requiredCapabilities so the runtime can reject requests against models that lack vision or file-input support before making network calls.

nodes.name: ChatBackend.scala
nodes.summary: Defines ChatBackend[F], the provider-neutral trait that every LLM provider backend must implement, with both plain and trace-aware chat overloads.
nodes.languageNotes: The trace-aware overload defaults to the un-traced one so existing backends keep compiling; backends that want to propagate correlation IDs override it.

nodes.name: ChatBackendLaws.scala
nodes.summary: Defines provider-neutral correctness laws for ChatBackend implementations, verifying response invariants, message ordering, tool round-trips, and finish-reason membership in the closed set.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses Scala 3 object with opaque law methods; designed to be called from munit FunSuite backends without wiring a real network.

nodes.name: checkResponseInvariants
nodes.summary: Validates that a ChatResponse is internally consistent: response.text matches message text, and finish reason belongs to the closed FinishReason set.

nodes.name: checkMessageOrderPreserved
nodes.summary: Verifies that the transport observes user message roles in the same order they appear in the ChatRequest.

nodes.name: checkToolsRoundTrip
nodes.summary: Verifies that tool schemas registered in a ChatRequest are faithfully reflected in the set observed by the transport layer.

nodes.name: ChatProtocol.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the core chat protocol types: the ChatMessage ADT (system/user/assistant/tool-result variants), ChatRequest with tool and format options, and ChatResponse carrying the AI message and usage metadata.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala 3 sealed trait hierarchy for ChatMessage; ChatRequest carries a requiredCapabilities computed field that introspects content types.

nodes.name: ChatTranscript.scala
nodes.summary: Provides ChatTranscript, a structured view of a conversation that separates the optional system prompt from turn messages, with correct multi-system-message merging and round-trip conversion to flat wire format.

nodes.name: fromMessages
nodes.summary: Splits a flat List[ChatMessage] into a ChatTranscript by extracting and merging system messages and preserving non-system turn order.

nodes.name: InvocationContext.scala
nodes.summary: Defines InvocationContext, a cross-cutting value carrying turn number, the originating ChatRequest, the specific ToolCall, and a TraceContext, passed to every tool executor and guardrail.

nodes.name: JsonSchema.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the JsonSchema ADT covering object, string, integer, number, boolean, array, enum, ref, and anyOf schema variants used for typed tool parameter and structured-output schema descriptions.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala 3 sealed trait with 8 case class variants; ObjectSchema runtime-validates required subsets of properties keys.

nodes.name: ModelMetadata.scala
nodes.summary: Declares the ModelCapability enum, ModelCapabilities helper for capability validation against a ChatRequest, Usage token-count type, UnsupportedModelCapabilities error, and FinishReason enum.

nodes.name: ModelPricing.scala
nodes.summary: Provides ModelPricing data and a calculateCost utility that looks up per-million-token pricing for known GPT and Gemini model families and computes total cost for a given token usage.

nodes.name: calculateCost
nodes.summary: Looks up per-million token pricing for a model name via longest-prefix matching, then computes total cost for given input and output token counts.

nodes.name: ResponseFormat.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the ResponseFormat sealed trait with Text and JsonSchema variants, used in ChatRequest to request plain text or structured JSON output from the model.

nodes.name: Tools.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the core tool-calling types: ToolSchema (description + parameter schema), ToolCall (name + arguments JSON), and the ToolResult ADT (Text, StructuredJson, Content variants).

nodes.name: TraceContext.scala
nodes.summary: Provides opaque TraceId and SpanId types and the TraceContext case class representing a trace-tree node, enabling OpenTelemetry-compatible correlation of concurrent chat invocations and nested tool/provider spans.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses Scala 3 opaque types for TraceId and SpanId to prevent accidental mix-ups while retaining String runtime representation.

nodes.name: ChatTranscriptSpec.scala
nodes.summary: munit FunSuite exercising ChatTranscript.fromMessages, toMessages, withTurn, withSystem, and withoutSystem across edge cases including positional and multi-system message scenarios.

nodes.name: CoreTypesSpec.scala
nodes.summary: munit FunSuite covering ChatMessage text extraction, ToolResult multimodal views, ModelCapabilities validation, ChatRequest capability inference, and ModelPricing cost calculation.

nodes.name: DocsLayoutSpec.scala
nodes.summary: munit FunSuite that guards the canonical documentation file layout (README.md, CHANGELOG.md, docs/USAGE.md) and verifies README links do not reference stale legacy paths or removed APIs.

nodes.name: AiAgentRunnable.scala
nodes.summary: Provides factory methods to lift an AiAgent into a Runnable[F, ChatRequest, String], either from an already-constructed agent or assembled from the RunContext's backend and config.

nodes.name: Assigned.scala
nodes.summary: Defines Assigned[In, Value], a covariant pair that carries a pipeline input alongside a computed output value, enabling merge combinator patterns in Runnable pipelines.

nodes.name: ChatModel.scala
nodes.summary: Provides a Runnable leaf that invokes the ChatBackend from RunContext, wrapping the provider request/response in onProviderRequest/onProviderResponse listener events with duration tracking.

nodes.name: ContentRetrieverRunnable.scala
nodes.summary: Wraps a ContentRetriever into a Runnable[F, String, List[RetrievedSource]] leaf node for integration into DSL retrieval pipelines.

nodes.name: Input.scala
nodes.summary: Provides identity and projection Runnable leaves (apply and pick) for lifting raw pipeline inputs into the DSL, serving as pipeline entry points.

nodes.name: PromptTemplate.scala
nodes.summary: Provides Runnable leaves for building ChatRequest from user input: user for plain prompt templates and retrievalAugmentedUser for RAG-augmented prompts that inline retrieved source context.

nodes.name: RetrievalAugmentorRunnable.scala
nodes.summary: Wraps a RetrievalAugmentor into a Runnable[F, ChatRequest, AugmentedChatRequest] leaf for integration into DSL RAG pipelines.

nodes.name: RunContext.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the RunContext[F] trait and DefaultRunContext implementation that carry the ChatBackend, RuntimeConfig, RuntimeListener, TraceContext, and optional StreamingChatBackend through a Runnable pipeline.

nodes.name: Runnable.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the core Runnable[F, In, Out] pipeline abstraction with combinators for sequential composition (andThen, |, >>), parallel execution (zipPar, par), projection (map, contramap), and graph description via RunnableGraph.
nodes.languageNotes: Heavily uses Scala 3 extension methods grouped by typeclass constraint (Functor, Monad, Parallel) to provide composable pipeline operators.

nodes.name: NamedRunnable
nodes.summary: A Runnable wrapper that attaches a user-supplied label to the graph node, enabling descriptive Mermaid diagram output.

nodes.name: RunnableGraph.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the RunnableGraph.Node ADT (Leaf, Unary, Binary) representing the structural topology of a pipeline, and provides a toMermaid renderer for visualizing the graph as a Mermaid diagram.

nodes.name: toMermaid
nodes.summary: Recursively traverses a RunnableGraph.Node tree, assigning sequential IDs to nodes, and produces a Mermaid graph TD diagram string.

nodes.name: StreamingChatModel.scala
nodes.summary: Provides a StreamingRunnable leaf that drives the StreamingChatBackend from RunContext, emitting StreamEvents via fs2.Stream and firing onStreamStarted/onStreamCompleted/onStreamFailed listener callbacks with token counts and durations.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses cats-effect Ref and Resource.ExitCase to safely track event counts and dispatch lifecycle callbacks across success, error, and cancellation outcomes.

nodes.name: StreamingRunnable.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the StreamingRunnable[F, In, Out] trait backed by fs2.Stream, with a leaf factory, graph description extensions, and andThenStream/mapStream combinators for composing streaming pipeline stages.

nodes.name: StructuredParser.scala
nodes.summary: Provides a DSL terminal node that decodes raw LLM text output into a typed value A using a StructuredCodec, raising an error on decode failure.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses Scala 3 context bounds (MonadThrow, StructuredCodec given) and matches Either decode results.

nodes.name: TextOutput.scala
nodes.summary: Provides a DSL terminal node that extracts the plain text string from a ChatResponse, bridging the chat model output to a String-typed chain.

nodes.name: WorkflowRunnable.scala
nodes.summary: Adapts agentic Workflow and WorkflowAgent instances into DSL Runnable nodes, enabling embedding of stateful orchestration inside typed chain compositions.
nodes.languageNotes: Three factory methods on the companion object cover fresh-scope, agent shorthand, and caller-provided shared scope variants.

nodes.name: ChatModelSpec.scala
nodes.summary: Integration tests for the ChatModel, PromptTemplate, TextOutput, StructuredParser, and AiAgentRunnable DSL nodes, covering chain composition, trace propagation, and listener event firing.

nodes.name: RagDslSpec.scala
nodes.summary: Tests for the RAG DSL layer including ContentRetrieverRunnable, RetrievalAugmentorRunnable, and the assign combinator, verifying retrieval, augmentation, and typed pairing semantics.

nodes.name: RunnableSpec.scala
nodes.summary: Unit tests for core Runnable combinators (map, contramap, named, zipPar) and Mermaid graph rendering, validating typed composition and parallel cancellation behavior.

nodes.name: RunnableSpecSupport.scala
nodes.summary: Shared test fixture providing a stubContext RunContext that raises an error on any backend call, used as a safe default context in DSL runnable specs.

nodes.name: StreamingRunnableSpec.scala
nodes.summary: Tests for the streaming DSL path (StreamingChatModel, andThenStream), verifying prompt template composition with fs2 streaming and listener lifecycle events (started, completed).

nodes.name: WorkflowRunnableSpec.scala
nodes.summary: Tests for WorkflowRunnable verifying fresh-scope isolation per run, shared-scope accumulation across calls, and in-run scope sharing between chained workflow agents.

nodes.name: GuardedChatBackend.scala
nodes.summary: Decorator ChatBackend that runs a GuardrailChain before and after the underlying backend call, with optional retry support via RetryPolicy.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses cats Parallel for concurrent guardrail execution and cats MonadThrow for error propagation.

nodes.name: GuardedChatBackend
nodes.summary: Final class wrapping a ChatBackend with input/output guardrail checks and configurable retry logic.

nodes.name: GuardedToolKit.scala
nodes.summary: Factory that wraps each tool executor in a GuardrailChain check, returning a structured JSON error result instead of raising when a tool call is blocked.

nodes.name: GuardrailChain.scala
nodes.summary: Core orchestration class for input, output, and tool guardrails supporting both sequential (transformation-preserving) and parallel (validator-only) evaluation modes.
nodes.languageNotes: Supports both sequential foldLeft-based chaining (preserving transformations) and parTraverse-based parallel checking; listener notifications fire before the exception is raised.

nodes.name: GuardrailChain
nodes.summary: Final case class holding ordered lists of input, output, and tool guardrails along with an optional listener, exposing sequential and parallel check methods.

nodes.name: GuardrailListener.scala
nodes.summary: Observability hook trait for the guardrail layer, fired when input, output, or tool guardrails block a request, with a noop default and a Default abstract base.

nodes.name: GuardrailResult.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the sealed GuardrailResult ADT (Allow/Block), GuardrailViolation data class, and GuardrailBlockedException for propagating blocked-request errors.
nodes.languageNotes: GuardrailResult is covariant (+A) so Block extends GuardrailResult[Nothing] and Allow[A] extends GuardrailResult[A].

nodes.name: Guardrails.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the core guardrail traits InputGuardrail, OutputGuardrail, and ToolGuardrail as the public extension points for custom policy implementations.

nodes.name: ModerationModel.scala
nodes.summary: Provides the ModerationModel trait and ModerationGuardrails factory that creates InputGuardrail and OutputGuardrail instances backed by a content moderation model.

nodes.name: RetryPolicy.scala
nodes.summary: Simple retry policy data class with configurable attempt count and error predicate, used by GuardedChatBackend to re-execute failed backend calls.

nodes.name: GuardrailListenerSpec.scala
nodes.summary: Tests that GuardrailChain fires the appropriate GuardrailListener callbacks (onInputBlocked, onOutputBlocked, onToolBlocked) before raising, and that the absent listener path raises without side effects.

nodes.name: GuardrailsSpec.scala
nodes.summary: Comprehensive integration tests for GuardedChatBackend, GuardedToolKit, ModerationGuardrails, RetryPolicy, and GuardrailChain parallel/sequential modes using local stub implementations.

nodes.name: HttpMcpTransport.scala
nodes.summary: HTTP implementation of McpTransport that sends JSON-RPC requests over sttp, tracks request IDs atomically via Ref, and validates response ID correlation.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses sttp client3 with a configurable SttpBackend[F, Any], making it backend-agnostic (works with any cats-effect compatible sttp backend).

nodes.name: HttpMcpTransport
nodes.summary: HTTP JSON-RPC transport for MCP using sttp, managing atomic request IDs and validating response correlation.

nodes.name: McpClient.scala
nodes.summary: High-level MCP client class providing listTools, listAllTools (with cursor-based pagination), and callTool operations over a McpTransport.
nodes.languageNotes: listAllTools uses recursive cursor pagination; callTool normalises non-object JSON arguments to {"value": ...} for MCP compliance.

nodes.name: McpClient
nodes.summary: Typed client for the MCP protocol supporting tool listing with cursor pagination and tool invocation over a McpTransport.

nodes.name: McpProtocol.scala
nodes.summary: Defines MCP wire-format data types (McpTool, McpToolList, McpContent, McpToolCallResult) and the McpProtocol codec object for building JSON-RPC payloads and decoding responses.
nodes.languageNotes: McpContent is a sealed ADT with Text/Image/File/Unknown variants, each mapping to an AiContent type used by the core layer.

nodes.name: McpSchemaConverter.scala
nodes.summary: Converts MCP ujson.Obj tool input schemas to the project's internal JsonSchema ADT, handling object, array, primitive, enum, anyOf, and $ref variants.
nodes.languageNotes: Recursive toSchema function handles all JsonSchema variants; toObjectSchema coerces non-object schemas to an empty ObjectSchema safely.

nodes.name: McpToolProvider.scala
nodes.summary: Bridges the MCP layer to the runtime ToolKit by fetching all tools from an McpClient, converting schemas, and creating McpToolExecutor wrappers for each tool.

nodes.name: McpTransport.scala
nodes.summary: Minimal transport trait for MCP defining a single request method that sends a JSON-RPC method with optional params and returns a result value.

nodes.name: StdioMcpTransport.scala
nodes.summary: Implements the McpTransport interface over stdio by serializing JSON-RPC requests to a writeLine function and reading responses from a readLine function, with mutex-based serialization for concurrent callers.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses cats-effect Ref and Mutex for thread-safe sequential request handling under the F[_] effect type.

nodes.name: StdioMcpTransport
nodes.summary: Concrete MCP transport that serializes JSON-RPC requests over a stdio line-oriented channel, using a mutex to prevent interleaved reads/writes during concurrent calls.

nodes.name: McpClientSpec.scala
nodes.summary: Test suite covering McpClient pagination, tool adapter, result mapping, and transport behaviour including StdioMcpTransport concurrency serialization and HttpMcpTransport id validation.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses a RecordingTransport helper that replays scripted ujson responses and records calls, and a hand-rolled SttpMonadError[IO] to stub the HTTP backend.

nodes.name: ChatMemory.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the ChatMemory[F[_], Id] trait providing effectful get, replace, and append operations for per-session conversation history keyed by an opaque Id.
nodes.languageNotes: Generic over both effect F[_] and key Id — callers choose their own session identifier type (e.g. MemoryId, String, UUID).

nodes.name: InMemoryChatMemory.scala
nodes.summary: Provides an in-process ChatMemory implementation backed by a cats-effect Ref[F, Map[Id, List[ChatMessage]]], suitable for testing and single-node deployments.
nodes.languageNotes: Overrides append atomically on the Ref to avoid the read-modify-write race present in the default trait implementation.

nodes.name: InMemoryChatMemory
nodes.summary: Concrete in-memory ChatMemory backed by a single Ref holding a keyed map of message lists, with an atomic append override.

nodes.name: MemoryAwareRuntime.scala
nodes.summary: Wraps an AiRuntime with a ChatMemory to produce history-threaded conversations, automatically loading prior messages before each chat call and persisting only the new conversation turns afterward, with optional observability via RuntimeListener.
nodes.languageNotes: Deliberately placed in llm4s-memory (not llm4s-runtime) so the core runtime module has no dependency on the memory abstraction layer.

nodes.name: MemoryAwareRuntime
nodes.summary: History-threading wrapper around AiRuntime that loads, injects, and persists conversation turns per memory ID, firing onMemoryRead and onMemoryWritten listener events for distributed tracing.

nodes.name: MemoryId.scala
nodes.summary: Defines MemoryId, a value-class wrapper around a String for identifying a conversation session in the memory module.

nodes.name: MessageWindowMemory.scala
nodes.summary: Decorator over ChatMemory that enforces a sliding window by retaining only the most recent maxMessages entries on every write, preventing unbounded memory growth in long conversations.

nodes.name: MessageWindowMemory
nodes.summary: ChatMemory decorator that trims stored message lists to a configured maximum window size on every replace or append call.

nodes.name: ChatMemorySpec.scala
nodes.summary: Tests InMemoryChatMemory session isolation and MessageWindowMemory trim-to-size behaviour using cats-effect IO.

nodes.name: MemoryAwareRuntimeSpec.scala
nodes.summary: Verifies MemoryAwareRuntime correctly threads conversation history across multiple chat calls and does not persist system prompts, using a scripted RecordingBackend stub.

nodes.name: AhcOpenAiStreamingTransport.scala
nodes.summary: Implements OpenAiStreamingTransport using async-http-client to push SSE body fragments into an unbounded fs2 queue, converting the callback-driven AHC API into a typed fs2.Stream[F, String].
nodes.languageNotes: Bridges async-http-client's callback model to cats-effect using a Dispatcher and Deferred for outcome signalling; cancellation is delegated to the Future returned by AHC's execute.

nodes.name: AhcOpenAiStreamingTransport
nodes.summary: SSE streaming transport that issues an AHC POST request and feeds body byte chunks into an fs2 queue as they arrive, decoding UTF-8 lines for downstream SSE parsing.

nodes.name: HttpListener.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the HttpListener[F] observability hook for HTTP-layer events (request, response, failure) fired by transports, with a noop implementation and a Default abstract class for partial overrides.

nodes.name: OpenAiCompatBackend.scala
nodes.summary: ChatBackend implementation for OpenAI-compatible APIs that delegates request encoding and response decoding to OpenAiWire and HTTP transport to OpenAiTransport, with factory methods for Resource-managed sttp backend lifetime.

nodes.name: OpenAiCompatBackend
nodes.summary: Concrete ChatBackend that encodes requests via OpenAiWire, forwards them through an OpenAiTransport with auth headers, and decodes the response.

nodes.name: OpenAiCompatConfig.scala
nodes.summary: Defines OpenAiCompatConfig case class with base URL, API key, model name, and per-request timeout, alongside the ResponseFormatMode enum controlling how response_format is emitted on the wire for compatibility with older OpenAI-compatible servers.
nodes.languageNotes: The ResponseFormatMode enum documents the three wire-compatibility levels (JsonSchema, JsonObject, Disabled) introduced in PR-18 to support older local runtimes.

nodes.name: OpenAiCompatStreamingBackend.scala
nodes.summary: StreamingChatBackend implementation that sets stream=true in the OpenAI wire request, delegates to OpenAiStreamingTransport for SSE lines, and decodes each line via OpenAiStreamDecoder.

nodes.name: OpenAiCompatStreamingBackend
nodes.summary: Streaming ChatBackend that encodes the request with stream=true, transports it through OpenAiStreamingTransport, and decodes SSE lines into StreamEvent values.

nodes.name: OpenAiStreamDecoder.scala
nodes.summary: Stateless SSE line decoder that parses OpenAI-format data: lines into StreamEvent values (TextDelta, ThinkingDelta, ToolCallDelta, Completed), silently skipping malformed or framing-only lines.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses scala.util.Try to swallow JSON parse failures from partial SSE chunks, keeping the stream alive rather than failing fast.

nodes.name: OpenAiStreamingTransport.scala
nodes.summary: Trait defining the OpenAiStreamingTransport[F] interface for SSE-based HTTP streaming, with a trace-aware overload that defaults to the un-traced variant.

nodes.name: OpenAiTransport.scala
nodes.summary: Trait defining the OpenAiTransport[F] interface for single request-response HTTP POST, with a trace-aware overload that falls back to the un-traced version for backwards compatibility.

nodes.name: OpenAiWire.scala
nodes.summary: Central OpenAI wire codec containing encodeChatRequest (ChatRequest → ujson.Obj with full message, tool, schema, and metadata mapping) and decodeChatResponse (ujson.Value → ChatResponse), handling multimodal content, tool calls, usage, and three response_format modes.
nodes.languageNotes: Contains many private helpers for individual ADT branches (encodeSchema, encodeContents, decodeContents, encodeToolCall, decodeToolCall) keeping the public surface to two functions.

nodes.name: encodeChatRequest
nodes.summary: Encodes a ChatRequest into an OpenAI-compatible ujson.Obj, conditionally including tools, response_format (controlled by ResponseFormatMode), temperature, and metadata.

nodes.name: decodeChatResponse
nodes.summary: Decodes an OpenAI-compatible JSON response into a ChatResponse, extracting message content, tool calls, finish reason, usage, response ID, and model name.

nodes.name: SttpOpenAiTransport.scala
nodes.summary: OpenAiTransport implementation backed by sttp that fires HttpListener events keyed by TraceContext around each POST, and maps HTTP error status codes to typed OpenAiHttpError subtypes.
nodes.languageNotes: Also defines the OpenAiHttpError ADT (Unauthorized, Forbidden, RateLimited, Client, Server) and the DefaultReadTimeout constant of 5 minutes for slow local models.

nodes.name: SttpOpenAiTransport
nodes.summary: sttp-backed transport that sends a JSON POST, records request/response/failure events on the HttpListener, and raises typed OpenAiHttpError on non-2xx responses.

nodes.name: TracedSttpBackend.scala
nodes.summary: SttpBackend decorator that wraps any SttpBackend to emit HttpListener events (request, response, failure) around each send, adding HTTP-layer tracing without modifying other transport wiring.
nodes.languageNotes: Mints a fresh TraceContext per HTTP call since it has no access to the chat-level TraceContext; for correlated tracing, prefer SttpOpenAiTransport with an HttpListener directly.

nodes.name: TracedSttpBackend
nodes.summary: SttpBackend decorator that fires HttpListener events on every request, measuring duration and forwarding failures before re-raising them.

nodes.name: JsonSchemaWireRoundTripSpec.scala
nodes.summary: Structural round-trip tests verifying that every JsonSchema ADT variant (StringSchema, IntegerSchema, NumberSchema, ArraySchema, ObjectSchema, EnumSchema, AnyOfSchema, RefSchema) encodes the correct wire JSON fields via OpenAiWire.

nodes.name: OpenAiBackendLawsSpec.scala
nodes.summary: Provider-neutral conformance test that uses ChatBackendLaws to verify message ordering, tool schema round-trip, and response invariants for OpenAiCompatBackend with a capturing transport stub.

nodes.name: OpenAiCompatBackendResourceSpec.scala
nodes.summary: Integration tests for OpenAiCompatBackend and OpenAiCompatStreamingBackend including Resource lifetime verification, requestTimeout propagation, real SSE streaming over a local HTTP server, and non-2xx error mapping.
nodes.languageNotes: Spins up a real com.sun.net.httpserver.HttpServer on a random port for the SSE streaming tests to exercise the full AHC transport path.

nodes.name: OpenAiCompatBackendSpec.scala
nodes.summary: Unit tests for OpenAiWire encoding and decoding covering model fields, response_format modes, tool_calls array wiring, tool-result name field (Gemini compat), multimodal content, usage decoding, and auth header handling.

nodes.name: OpenAiCompatStreamingBackendSpec.scala
nodes.summary: Tests OpenAiStreamDecoder line parsing and OpenAiCompatStreamingBackend request wiring, verifying stream=true is set, events are decoded correctly, and Authorization headers are omitted when apiKey is empty.

nodes.name: OpenAiStreamDecoderCorpusSpec.scala
nodes.summary: Corpus-style test suite for the OpenAI SSE streaming decoder, feeding realistic provider-captured chunks through `OpenAiStreamDecoder.decodeLine` and asserting correct event emission for text deltas, tool call deltas, finish reasons, and malformed inputs.

nodes.name: TracedSttpBackendSpec.scala
nodes.summary: Test suite verifying `TracedSttpBackend` fires HTTP lifecycle events (request, response, failure) through `HttpListener`, that TraceContext is propagated from the chat runtime to HTTP events, and that read timeouts are forwarded to outgoing sttp requests.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses cats-effect IO with `unsafeRunSync` in munit tests; inline sttp backend stubs avoid any real network traffic.

nodes.name: AdvancedContentRetriever.scala
nodes.summary: Implements the full RAG retrieval pipeline: query transformation, multi-source routing via `QueryRouter`, result aggregation with deduplication, and re-ranking before returning the top-N results.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses cats `traverse` for effectful fan-out over multiple transformed queries and routed retrievers.

nodes.name: AdvancedContentRetriever
nodes.summary: Orchestrates transform → route → aggregate → re-rank steps to produce a final ranked list of retrieved sources for a query.

nodes.name: ContentAggregator.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the `ContentAggregator` trait and a default implementation that deduplicates retrieved sources by ID, keeping the best score and merging metadata from all duplicates.

nodes.name: ContentRetriever.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the `ContentRetriever[F]` trait as the core retrieval abstraction, and provides `EmbeddingContentRetriever` which embeds a query text and delegates to an `EmbeddingStore` to perform similarity search.

nodes.name: EmbeddingModel.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the `EmbeddingModel[F]` trait with a single `embed` method plus a default `embedAll` batch helper using cats `Applicative`.

nodes.name: EmbeddingStore.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the `EmbeddingStore[F]` trait for persisting and searching embedding records, with `add`, `search`, and `remove` operations.

nodes.name: EmbeddingVector.scala
nodes.summary: Value-class wrapping a `Vector[Double]` with cosine similarity, normalization, and pgvector literal serialization methods for use throughout the RAG pipeline.

nodes.name: EmbeddingVector
nodes.summary: Dense floating-point vector supporting cosine similarity computation, L2 normalization, and serialization to PostgreSQL pgvector literal format.

nodes.name: InMemoryEmbeddingStore.scala
nodes.summary: Thread-safe in-memory `EmbeddingStore` backed by a cats-effect `Ref`, performing cosine similarity ranking and supporting namespace and metadata filtering — intended for testing and development use.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses cats-effect `Ref` for thread-safe mutable state inside `F[_]: Sync`.

nodes.name: InMemoryEmbeddingStore
nodes.summary: In-memory implementation of `EmbeddingStore` using normalized cosine similarity; supports namespace scoping and metadata predicate filtering.

nodes.name: PgVectorEmbeddingStore.scala
nodes.summary: Production-grade `EmbeddingStore` backed by PostgreSQL with the pgvector extension, supporting upsert, cosine-distance ANN search, namespace and metadata filtering, safe SQL identifier validation, and table initialization.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses JDBC via `DataSource` with `Sync[F].blocking` for all DB calls; SQL identifiers are validated by regex before interpolation to prevent injection.

nodes.name: PgVectorEmbeddingStore
nodes.summary: JDBC-backed embedding store using pgvector's cosine-distance operator for ANN search, with compiled metadata filter SQL and namespace encoding.

nodes.name: QueryRouter.scala
nodes.summary: Defines `QueryRouter[F]` for routing a query to one or more `ContentRetriever` instances, with `static` (fixed list) and `from` (custom function) factory constructors.

nodes.name: QueryTransformer.scala
nodes.summary: Defines `QueryTransformer[F]` for expanding or rewriting a user query into multiple queries, with `identity` (pass-through) and `static` (function-based) factory constructors.

nodes.name: ReRanker.scala
nodes.summary: Defines `ReRanker[F]` for reordering retrieved sources after aggregation, with `identity` (preserve order) and `byScore` (sort descending by score) factory constructors.

nodes.name: RetrievalAugmentor.scala
nodes.summary: Defines `RetrievalAugmentor[F]` and `DefaultRetrievalAugmentor`, which retrieves context for the last user message in a `ChatRequest` and injects a rendered context block into the message before returning the augmented request alongside retrieved sources.

nodes.name: DefaultRetrievalAugmentor
nodes.summary: Augments a `ChatRequest` by retrieving context for the last user message and prepending a rendered source block to the query text.

nodes.name: RetrievalQuery.scala
nodes.summary: Defines `RetrievalQuery` (vector + search parameters) and the `MetadataFilter` ADT supporting `Eq`, `In`, `And`, and `Or` predicates used by both in-memory and pgvector stores.

nodes.name: RetrievedSource.scala
nodes.summary: Defines `EmbeddingRecord` (the stored form of a document with its embedding) and `RetrievedSource` (the retrieval result carrying id, text, score, and metadata).

nodes.name: RagSpec.scala
nodes.summary: Integration-level test suite for the llm4s-rag module, covering in-memory store ranking, embedding retriever, namespace/metadata filtering, retrieval augmentation, pgvector config validation, content aggregation, and the full advanced retriever pipeline.

nodes.name: AiRuntime.scala
nodes.summary: Core chat runtime that drives a multi-turn `ChatBackend` loop using stack-safe `tailRecM`, dispatching tool calls via `ToolLoop`, enforcing turn limits, and firing `RuntimeListener` lifecycle events with trace correlation.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses `tailRecM` for stack-safety across arbitrary tool-call turns; `Parallel` constraint enables concurrent tool execution in `ToolLoop`.

nodes.name: AiRuntime
nodes.summary: Drives a multi-turn LLM chat loop: builds requests, calls the backend, handles tool calls, enforces max turns, and emits observability events via RuntimeListener.

nodes.name: AiRuntimeError.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the `AiRuntimeError` sealed hierarchy of typed exceptions covering `MaxTurnsExceeded`, `ContentFiltered`, `ProviderError`, `ToolMissing`, and `ToolFailed` for pattern-matchable error handling in the chat runtime.

nodes.name: InvocationContext.scala
nodes.summary: Re-exports `InvocationContext` from `llm4s-core` for backwards compatibility, and defines `RuntimeConfig` (max turns and tool error policies) plus the `ToolErrorPolicy` enum.

nodes.name: RuntimeListener.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the `RuntimeListener[F]` observability trait with hooks for chat, provider, tool, memory, and streaming lifecycle events, including span bracket methods for distributed tracing integration; provides `noop` and `Default` base implementations.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses higher-kinded `F[_]` with `Applicative` for no-op defaults; `Default` abstract class lets adopters override only the events they care about without breaking on future additions.

nodes.name: ToolKit.scala
nodes.summary: Defines `ToolKit[F]` as a Map-backed bundle pairing `ToolSchema` with `ToolExecutor` by name, eliminating the previous footgun of mismatched schema/executor lists; provides factory constructors and merge operators.

nodes.name: ToolKit
nodes.summary: Immutable, name-indexed registry pairing each tool schema with its executor; supports merge, add-or-replace, and backward-compatible construction.

nodes.name: ToolLoop.scala
nodes.summary: Executes all tool calls in a single chat turn concurrently using `parTraverse`, handling unknown tools and per-tool error policies (`FailFast`, `SurfaceToModel`, `RetryOnce`) while firing `RuntimeListener` events for each attempt.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses `parTraverse` from Cats `Parallel` to run tool calls concurrently while preserving the original call order in the result list.

nodes.name: AiRuntimeSpec.scala
nodes.summary: Comprehensive test suite for `AiRuntime` covering single-turn responses, tool execution, max-turn limit enforcement, content filter and provider error handling, stack-safety under thousands of turns, and concurrent parallel tool execution.

nodes.name: RuntimeListenerSpec.scala
nodes.summary: Exhaustive test suite for `RuntimeListener` v2 hooks, verifying trace ID propagation, per-turn provider event ordering, tool retry visibility, concurrent chat isolation, span bracket nesting order, and chat failure event delivery.

nodes.name: ToolErrorPolicySpec.scala
nodes.summary: Tests the three tool error policies (SurfaceToModel, FailFast, RetryOnce) and the unknown-tool policy variants of AiRuntime, verifying correct error propagation and recovery behaviour.

nodes.name: ToolKitSpec.scala
nodes.summary: Unit tests for ToolKit construction, validation, merging (++), and per-entry replacement, covering both the legacy and builder-style constructors.

nodes.name: StreamEvent.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the sealed StreamEvent ADT whose variants represent incremental streaming output: text deltas, thinking deltas, tool call fragments, completed tool calls, and a final completion event.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses a Scala 3 sealed trait hierarchy with final case class variants — the canonical ADT pattern for exhaustive pattern matching.

nodes.name: StreamingAiRuntime.scala
nodes.summary: Streaming counterpart to AiRuntime that wraps a StreamingChatBackend and emits RuntimeListener telemetry events (started/completed/failed) around the fs2 stream lifecycle.

nodes.name: StreamingAiRuntime
nodes.summary: Streaming counterpart to AiRuntime; wraps StreamingChatBackend[F] and emits RuntimeListener telemetry (started/completed/failed) bracketing the fs2 Stream lifecycle.

nodes.name: StreamingChatBackend.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the StreamingChatBackend trait, the single-method interface that provider implementations must satisfy to supply a ChatRequest-to-StreamEvent stream.

nodes.name: StreamSubscriber.scala
nodes.summary: Minimal callback trait for code that wants to observe individual StreamEvents without consuming the underlying fs2 Stream directly.

nodes.name: TokenStream.scala
nodes.summary: Thin wrapper around a Stream[F, StreamEvent] that provides convenience accessors — extracting only text deltas as a String stream and collecting the full text via collectText.

nodes.name: StreamingAiRuntimeSpec.scala
nodes.summary: Tests StreamingAiRuntime behaviour: request construction, text-delta collection, RuntimeListener lifecycle events (started/completed/failed), and error propagation through the stream.

nodes.name: AiAgent.scala
nodes.summary: High-level facade over AiRuntime providing plain-text chat, typed structured chat (chatAs), memory-backed variants, and per-call option overrides; supports runtime sharing via withTools and runtime replacement via withConfig.

nodes.name: AiAgent

nodes.name: ChatOptions.scala
nodes.summary: Defines ChatOptions, a per-call override bag carrying optional toolkit, temperature, responseFormat, and metadata that AiAgent applies on top of its own defaults.

nodes.name: JsonExtractor.scala
nodes.summary: Extracts a parseable JSON value from arbitrary LLM output using a three-stage strategy: direct parse, markdown fence stripping, and balanced-brace scanning with string-literal awareness.
nodes.languageNotes: The balanced-brace scanner uses @tailrec to avoid stack overflow on long strings, carrying string/escape state through accumulator parameters.

nodes.name: extract
nodes.summary: Public entry point: tries direct parse, then fence-stripped parse, then balanced-block scan; returns Right(value) on first success or Left with an error preview.

nodes.name: scan

nodes.name: StructuredCodec.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the StructuredCodec typeclass bundling schema name, JsonSchema, and a decode function; provides a Scala 3 inline derivation that routes decoding through JsonExtractor for robustness against chatty model output.

nodes.name: StructuredOutputRuntime.scala
nodes.summary: Utility object providing chat and chatWithMemory methods that build a ResponseFormat.JsonSchema-bearing ChatRequest, delegate to AiRuntime, and decode the response with a StructuredCodec.

nodes.name: AiAgentSpec.scala

nodes.name: JsonExtractorSpec.scala

nodes.name: StructuredOutputRuntimeSpec.scala

nodes.name: SchemaEncoder.scala
nodes.summary: Typeclass that converts a Scala type to a JsonSchema; provides primitive givens, Option/List wrappers, and inline Scala 3 derivation for case classes (ObjectSchema) and enums (EnumSchema).

nodes.name: ToolDef.scala

nodes.name: ToolDefinition.scala
nodes.summary: Builder for ToolDefinition values that pairs a ToolSchema with a ToolExecutor; factory methods fromProduct and fromArgs decode typed arguments before dispatching to the user function, returning structured JSON errors on decode failure.

nodes.name: ValueDecoder.scala
nodes.summary: Typeclass for decoding a ujson.Value into a Scala type; provides primitive givens, Option/List combinators, and inline Scala 3 derivation for case classes and enums.

nodes.name: ToolDefinitionSpec.scala
nodes.summary: Integration tests for ToolDefinition, SchemaEncoder, ValueDecoder, and ToolDef derivation covering nested products, optional fields, lists, enums, argument decoding, and structured error responses.

nodes.name: NatchezHttpListener

nodes.name: NatchezRuntimeListener.scala

tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: The README is the front door to llm4s-chain: a Scala 3, cats-effect / sttp framework that gives you provider-neutral building blocks for LLM applications. Reading it first establishes the 14-module map — core protocol, provider backend, runtime, structured outputs, streaming, memory, RAG, MCP, agentic workflows, guardrails, tracing, and the high-level DSL — which is exactly the order the tour will explore. The USAGE.md companion doc provides the corresponding code examples for all 17 capability areas, so it is the reference you return to after each tour stop.

tour.title: Demo Entry Point
tour.description: AgentDemoMain is the cats-effect IOApp that wires everything together and is the recommended first file to run. It demonstrates three AiAgent usage patterns in sequence: plain chat, typed structured output decoded into a CvReview case class, and a tool-calling tutor agent with a WikiLookup tool. Starting here gives you an immediate end-to-end picture before descending into the abstractions that make it work.
tour.languageLesson: cats-effect IOApp replaces main(args: Array[String]): Unit with run: IO[ExitCode], giving the whole program a single managed effect boundary. Every resource (HTTP client, thread pool) is acquired and released safely via Resource.use, even when the JVM receives SIGINT.

tour.title: Backend Wiring & Config
tour.description: BackendSupport is the factory that constructs the full demo stack — OpenAI-compatible ChatBackend, ListenerBundle, and parsed AppConfig — as a single cats-effect Resource. AppConfig drives everything: it reads config.yaml to select the LLM provider, model, timeout, and per-component tracing verbosity. Understanding this wiring step explains how the demo binds a runtime configuration file to the live provider before any chat call is made.
tour.languageLesson: cats-effect Resource[F, A] models acquire-release lifecycles. Composing Resources with flatMap or the resource comprehension builds a dependency tree where teardown always happens in reverse acquisition order, even on error — eliminating the need for try/finally nesting.

tour.title: Core Protocol ADTs
tour.description: llm4s-core defines the vocabulary every other module speaks. ChatProtocol contains the ChatMessage ADT (system / user / assistant / tool-result variants), ChatRequest with tool and format options, and ChatResponse carrying the AI message plus usage metadata. ChatBackend[F] is the provider-neutral trait that every backend implements with a single chat method, ensuring the rest of the library never touches provider-specific wire formats. The JsonSchema ADT alongside it defines typed schemas used by both tool parameters and structured outputs.
tour.languageLesson: Scala 3 sealed traits with enum-style case classes form Algebraic Data Types (ADTs). The compiler enforces exhaustive pattern matching, so adding a new ChatMessage variant is a compile error in every match site — a property you cannot get with open class hierarchies.

tour.title: Tool Schema & Decoding
tour.description: llm4s-tools provides the typeclass layer that bridges Scala types and JSON tool schemas without any boilerplate. SchemaEncoder[A] derives a JsonSchema from a case class or enum via Scala 3 inline derivation, while ValueDecoder[A] decodes a ujson.Value back into that same type after the LLM executes the tool call. The companion Tools.scala in core defines ToolSchema, ToolCall, and the ToolResult ADT that these typeclasses feed into the runtime.
tour.languageLesson: Scala 3 inline derivation (inline given, Mirrors.ProductOf) lets the compiler generate typeclass instances at compile time without a macro. The derived SchemaEncoder for a case class walks the field types recursively, producing a nested JsonSchema that exactly mirrors the Scala type — no runtime reflection.

tour.title: Provider Backend
tour.description: llm4s-openai-compat implements ChatBackend[F] using sttp for HTTP and SSE. OpenAiCompatBackend constructs requests from ChatRequest, calls the provider endpoint, and decodes the response through OpenAiWire codecs — the uPickle read/write instances for the OpenAI JSON wire format. SttpOpenAiTransport handles the raw HTTP plumbing, while the streaming counterpart (OpenAiCompatStreamingBackend) emits token-level events via fs2 streams. Any OpenAI-compatible provider (Anthropic, Gemini, local models) plugs in here without touching the rest of the library.
tour.languageLesson: sttp is backend-agnostic: the same request description compiles against the async-http-client, Netty, or fs2 backends. OpenAiCompatBackend selects the backend at construction time, so switching from JVM to Scala.js requires only a different SttpBackend given — the request code is unchanged.

tour.title: Chat Runtime & Tool Loop
tour.description: AiRuntime is the execution engine that drives the chat loop: it sends a ChatRequest to the backend, collects any ToolCall responses, executes them concurrently through ToolKit, appends ToolResult messages, and loops until the model returns a text response. RuntimeListener provides the observability trait — hooks for chat start/complete, provider request/response, tool invocations, memory reads, and streaming events — so every layer of the runtime emits structured telemetry without coupling to any specific backend. InvocationContext (re-exported from core) carries the per-call trace and metadata through the loop.
tour.languageLesson: parTraverse in cats-effect runs all tool calls concurrently within a single chat turn. Because each ToolExecutor returns F[ToolResult] and F is IO, parallel execution is safe by construction — no shared mutable state, and cancellation propagates automatically if one tool call fails.

tour.title: AiAgent & Structured Outputs
tour.description: AiAgent (in llm4s-structured) is the high-level facade over AiRuntime that most application code will use directly. Its chatAs[A] method sends a prompt and decodes the response into a typed Scala value A using SchemaEncoder and JsonExtractor — the same pattern AgentDemoMain uses for CvReview. JsonExtractor applies a three-stage fallback strategy (direct parse, markdown fence strip, balanced-brace scan) to extract valid JSON from unpredictable LLM output, making structured output robust to model formatting quirks.

tour.title: Session Memory & RAG
tour.description: ChatMemory[F, Id] defines effectful get / replace / append operations for per-session conversation history keyed by an opaque identifier, enabling AiAgent's memory-backed chat variants. The RAG module extends this with ContentRetriever[F] — an abstraction over embedding-backed document search — and RetrievedSource, the result type carrying id, text, relevance score, and metadata. RetrievedSource has the highest fan-in of any node in the graph (8 inbound edges), reflecting how widely the DSL, retriever implementations, and augmentor modules all depend on this single type.
tour.languageLesson: Opaque types (opaque type Id = String) give zero-overhead type safety — the compiler prevents mixing a session Id with a plain String, but at runtime they are identical. This is the idiomatic Scala 3 replacement for newtype libraries and value classes.

tour.title: MCP Tool Integration
tour.description: llm4s-mcp implements the Model Context Protocol (MCP) JSON-RPC client, allowing the library to expose and call tools hosted by external MCP servers over stdio or HTTP transport. McpClient provides listTools, listAllTools (with cursor pagination), and callTool; McpProtocol defines the JSON-RPC message ADTs. Connecting an MCP server to AiRuntime's ToolKit makes any MCP-exposed tool available to the LLM without writing Scala glue code for each tool individually.

tour.title: Agentic Workflows
tour.description: llm4s-agentic introduces composable, deterministic multi-step workflows separate from the LLM's own reasoning. Workflow[F, In, Out] is the fundamental composable unit — a typed In => F[Out] computation. SequenceWorkflow, ParallelWorkflow, ConditionalWorkflow, and LoopWorkflow are concrete combinators that build complex control flow from simple pieces. SupervisorAgent sits above these: it uses the LLM to dynamically select sub-agents from a SubAgentRegistry and orchestrate them via a plan-execute loop, bridging deterministic composition with LLM-driven planning.
tour.languageLesson: LoopWorkflow uses tailRecM for stack-safe iteration inside F[_]. In cats-effect IO, tailRecM compiles the loop into a trampoline, so a loop running thousands of iterations never blows the JVM stack — a requirement for long-running agentic tasks.

tour.title: Guardrails & Tracing
tour.description: GuardrailChain wraps any ChatBackend with a composable sequence of pre- and post-call checks — content policy, retry policy, and moderation — returning GuardedChatBackend, which is itself a ChatBackend and therefore transparent to the rest of the stack. Distributed tracing integrates through NatchezRuntimeListener, a RuntimeListener implementation that bridges the library's observability hooks to Natchez spans; TracingWiring in the demo harness shows how to construct the full ListenerBundle (RuntimeListener + HttpListener + GuardrailListener + WorkflowListener) from a single TracingConfig.
tour.languageLesson: The decorator pattern in purely functional Scala uses type-matching: GuardedChatBackend extends ChatBackend[F], so it can be passed anywhere a ChatBackend is expected. Composing decorators (guardrail wrapping a traced backend wrapping the HTTP backend) requires no inheritance hierarchy — just function composition on the effect type.

tour.title: DSL Pipeline Composition
tour.description: Runnable[F, In, Out] is the capstone abstraction of the entire library: a typed pipeline node with sequential (andThen / >> / |) and parallel (zipPar / par) combinators, mirroring LangChain Expression Language (LCEL). ChatModel, PromptTemplate, StructuredParser, ContentRetrieverRunnable, and AiAgentRunnable are the leaf nodes; they compose into a RunnableGraph whose topology can be rendered as a Mermaid diagram via toMermaid. LCEL_DEMO and LCEL_OPERATOR_DEMO show the three canonical chain shapes: plain prompt-to-model, typed structured output, and RAG-augmented retrieval.
tour.languageLesson: Runnable[F, In, Out] is analogous to a Kleisli arrow (In => F[Out]) but richer: andThen composes Runnables like function composition, map transforms the output type, and contramap transforms the input — making Runnable simultaneously a Functor and a Contravariant Functor depending on which type parameter you vary.

tour.title: Build Definition
tour.description: build.sbt declares the multi-project structure that keeps modules independently compilable and testable. It wires llm4s-structured -> llm4s-runtime -> llm4s-openai-compat -> llm4s-core and so on, mirroring the conceptual layering of the tour. project/Dependencies.scala centralises all library versions (cats-effect, fs2, sttp, natchez, uPickle) so version bumps happen in one place. Understanding the build definition is essential when adding a new capability module or debugging a classpath issue.
tour.languageLesson: sbt multi-project builds use the dependsOn operator to express inter-module compilation order. Unlike Maven modules, sbt evaluates the dependency graph lazily and in parallel across independent modules, so a 14-module build like this compiles faster than a sequential Maven reactor.

tour.title: CI/CD Pipeline
tour.description: The GitHub Actions workflow runs on every push and pull request to main, executing scalafmt check, compile, test, and scoverage coverage reporting for all 14 sbt modules on Java 21 and Scala 3.3.4. The sbt dependency cache is keyed on build.sbt and Dependencies.scala, so incremental builds skip the 2-3 minute dependency download on most runs. This is the quality gate that enforces formatting, compilation, and test coverage standards across the entire multi-module library.
tour.languageLesson: GitHub Actions matrix builds let a single job definition run across multiple Scala or JDK versions in parallel. For a library, this is critical: a dependency upgrade that compiles on Scala 3.3 but not 3.4 is caught immediately rather than discovered by a downstream consumer.
